Hamper

HAM-per -- not related to the noun 'hamper' meaning a basket. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To hamper to hinder, delay, or interfere with the progress of something.

Heavy snowfall continued to hamper rescue efforts throughout the night.

Worked Example

A single flat tire forces an entire delivery truck to sit on the shoulder for two hours, throwing off the schedule for every other stop planned that day.

That slowing-down, getting-in-the-way effect is exactly what it means to hamper something. Unlike 'stop,' which ends progress completely, hamper means to slow it down or make it harder.

How Hamper Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

hinder

hinder: to create difficulties that delay or prevent an action

impede

impede: to delay or block the progress of something

obstruct

obstruct: to block or get in the way of something

Antonyms

facilitate

facilitate: to make an action or process easier

expedite

expedite: to make a process happen faster

How Strong Is It? — hinder → hamper → obstruct

hinder vs. hamper

hinder vs. hamper: Hinder is close in strength to hamper, though hamper often suggests an ongoing, nagging interference, while hinder can describe a single obstacle that gets in the way just once.

obstruct vs. hamper

obstruct vs. hamper: Obstruct can feel stronger than hamper: hamper usually means slowing something down, while obstruct suggests actively blocking it so it can't move forward at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — hamper-

root — hamper-: origin uncertain; possibly connected to Anglo-French 'hanaper,' a case used to confine and store cups tightly (Middle English (uncertain))

Put it together

Put it together: Hamper's exact origin is debated among etymologists, but it likely traces to Middle English hamperen, possibly connected to hanaper, a case used to store cups and confine them tightly. To hamper something, in that light, is to hem it in and keep it from moving freely.

Use the root in a new word: encumber

Use the root in a new word: encumber: Heavy backpacks can encumber hikers on the steepest parts of the trail.
